back: Real (anonymised) inputs, known failures, edge cases; reference or acceptance rule; tags for slicing; dev and held-out splits; versioned.
Deterministic checks, reference metrics (cheap, meaning-blind), LLM-as-judge (semantic, costly, biased).
Each score level is tied to observable behaviour, e.g. '5: correct, direct, cites source; 1: factual error'.
A pairwise judge may favour the first or second answer; run both orders and keep consistent verdicts.
Judges may favour longer text or text in their own style; control length, use a different judge model.
$d_i=b_i-a_i$ on the same item; the mean estimates the improvement and item difficulty cancels.
Resample items with replacement B times, recompute the mean difference, take the 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles.
Under H0 each non-zero difference is equally likely + or -; p = share of the 2^m sign patterns with |sum| at least the observed.
Flipping the sign of 0 changes nothing, so ties carry no information about which prompt is better.
Run the eval on every change; block if a check fails or the CI of the difference falls below an accepted margin.
Averages hide regressions: one tag can collapse while the mean rises.
Log inputs, outputs, tool calls, latency, cost, guardrail triggers; sample for review; track drift; add failures to the eval set.
